name: Sandbox Escape
tagline: A bug-bounty league for the universe's engine: pay compressors per joule saved, pay detectors only for transfer, and salt the real sky to turn 'are we simulated?' into a number with error bars.
summary: Sandbox Escape is a seasonal adversarial league that threat-models the universe's engine instead of hunting glitches. Red teams of humans and OpenEvolve-style optimizers build lattice universes that must pass a fidelity suite rescaled from the live Standard Model Extension bounds, and they earn bounty per joule saved against a reference engine, so the shortcuts come from real optimization pressure rather than taste. Hunters submit frozen, observables-only pipelines through mock instruments with injected systematics and are paid only when their detections transfer to held-out engine families. Each season ends with a salted round: the winning engines' fingerprints are injected into enclave copies of real Fermi-LAT (later Auger) data, so recovered salts calibrate each pipeline and the clean run yields a real bound. The outputs are a cost-detectability frontier, calibrated bounds on new physics, a 'price list for physics' in a classical-host column, and the same frontier read the other way, measuring how cheap a sandbox can be before an AI agent notices it is in one.
core_loop: Red teams commit hashed lattice engines that pass a rescaled fidelity suite and get paid per joule saved -> hunters probe through observables-only mock instruments and pre-register claims -> sources open and claims are log-scored, paying only for transfer to held-out engine families built by a tasteless evolutionary optimizer -> a salted round injects winning fingerprints into enclave copies of real archives, and frozen pipelines run over salted and clean copies -> recovered salts calibrate sensitivity and clean results become real bounds -> tightened real bounds update the fidelity suite, outlawing that slack next season.
why_now: Generative world models have made 'simulated worlds with agents inside' an engineering object, and simulation-theory papers keep appearing with no shared test protocol. AI scientists run closed experimental loops and long METR task horizons let an agent run a whole campaign. AlphaEvolve-style evolutionary coding agents supply a compressor with no taste, only cost pressure. Labs now need to know whether agents can tell they are being evaluated, which is the same frontier seen from the other side.
mvp: 90 days on public data. Weeks 1-3: a JAX reference engine (scalar + U(1) on a 3+1D lattice), mock Fermi-like photon-timing and Auger-like arrival-map instruments with injected systematics, and a fidelity suite rescaled to explored dynamic range. Weeks 4-6: 12 engines in three families, half human-built, half OpenEvolve-built, all run at three sizes on identical GPUs with energy metering. Weeks 7-10: round 1, with hunters' containers scored on a held-out family. Weeks 11-12: the first salted round, on Fermi GRB timing only, inside an enclave. Kill metrics: no engine saves 10% energy while passing fidelity, or salt recovery is under 50%.
stack: JAX lattice field engines on identical GPUs with per-run energy metering; OpenEvolve (AlphaEvolve-style) as the evolutionary compressor; signed source-hash commits; gVisor-sandboxed hunter containers in a Kaggle-code-competition-style enclave returning scores only; public Fermi-LAT photon data and the Auger open-data fraction; log scoring of pre-registered claims; scaling-curve fits across engine sizes.
business_model: Foundational-physics funders (FQXi, Templeton) pay for the physics side. The paying customers are sim-to-real and AI safety. Robotics teams training in Isaac or Genie-style world models need to know which simulator artefacts a policy can detect, and labs need to know how cheap a sandbox can be before a model notices it. Simulator vendors and labs sponsor seasons, buy audits and fund bounties paid in compute.
risks: Detectors may not transfer across engine families, which would stop the port before it starts
Scaling from a 10^3 toy dynamic range to our universe's 10^60 is a hypothesis, so curves must be published as hypotheses, never as bounds
Auger data access is political; only Fermi-LAT is fully public
Payoffs are mostly null bounds, which strains funding and attention
Crank capture and 'league finds glitch' headlines; mitigated by coordinated disclosure to instrument collaborations under a 90-day embargo
Red-hunter collusion and leaked salts; mitigated by signed commits, side separation and enclave-only scoring
It is a training gym for AI evaluation awareness; hunter APIs expose physics observables only, and frontier-agent results go to eval teams before publication
FLOP accounting can be gamed; mitigated by paying per joule on identical hardware
moonshot: By 2036 fault-tolerant quantum machines run quantum-host engines and fill the price list's second column. The league publishes a host-complexity bound, the cheapest host consistent with every measurement humanity has made, and it rises each time an experiment tightens a bound. Physics collaborations pre-register analyses on the bounty board as routine, and 'are we simulated?' stops being a belief and becomes a number with error bars.
best_line: Expensive laws are anti-fingerprints; a thrifty classical implementer wouldn't pay for them.
